answer: Complementary-Slope Admission Filter.** Each agent must submit a short yarrow-marked workload trace at registration; the system checks that its resource-use slope complements, rather than mirrors, existing traces, rejecting near-duplicates. A violet flag marks clusters whose traces overlap beyond a set similarity, forcing re-verification. Because a lagoon of cloned agents shares one slope, attackers must generate genuinely distinct behavioral traces per identity, paying real compute and instrumentation cost for each fake participant.
